user.job: choose the storage and lifecycle substrate for the ZKC MVP that can hold dual-track static/dynamic knowledge, model its lifecycle and decay, and run locally under scarce attention

baseline.workflow: no substrate chosen yet; prior coverage research concluded no OSS knowledge app is a drop-in replacement and that dual-track capture plus attention scheduling must be built in-house
failureModes: no temporal/validity model for evolving facts
substrate may require a server, breaking offline capture
graph+vector+temporal split across stores increases complexity

targetOutcome: select one MVP storage substrate and state explicitly which lifecycle/versioning/decay semantics ZKC must own in the application schema
goals: compare storage candidates on T1.1 / T1.2 / T1.3
determine whether decay and bitemporal modeling can be delegated to the store
recommend a substrate with a swappable seam
nonGoals: do not build the ZKC storage layer in this step
do not benchmark throughput or latency
do not solve multi-device sync for MVP

constraints.statement: personal data; privacy and offline operation preferred
prefer minimal runtime dependencies for a solo-dev MVP
findings pinned to a sealed ledger snapshot on 2026-10-28

assumptions: stars and topicMatch are discovery signals, not capability scores
Postgres is acceptable as a local dependency
graph traversal for MVP is shallow enough for recursive CTEs
decisionScope: storage substrate selection for the ZKC architecture

options.name: Kuzu embedded graph with vector search
